title: How to Help Your Teen Apologize Without Writing the Apology for Them
summary: Coach your teen to own the harm, ask what repair would help, do the practical work, and deliver the apology themselves without forcing forgiveness or contact.
seo_description: Use four clear steps to help your teen own a mistake, apologise, and repair peer harm without writing the message, forcing forgiveness, or taking over.
release_move: The parent holds safety and household boundaries, coaches the structure of repair, and leaves the apology's words, delivery, and reasonable repair work to the teen.

core_belief_shift.from: A good apology requires me to supply the right words and make sure my teen sends them.
core_belief_shift.to: I can require accountability and coach repair while leaving the apology and its delivery to my teen.

book_relevance.reason: The Social Playbook, Chapter 12, gives teens optional practice in admitting a mistake without excuses and asking how to repair it; this parent guide remains complete without the book.

hero.alt: A teenager writes an apology on her own phone while her father sits nearby, attentive without taking over.

social_image.alt: A teenager writes an apology on her own phone while her father sits nearby, attentive without taking over.
